extracted.intended_audience: designers, data-visualization practitioners, marketers, and novices seeking guidance on creating infographics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing infographics and data visualizations that communicate data clearly and memorably across formats (online, print, presentations), including storytelling, design process, and release/SEO strategy. Targeted to both novices and experienced professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: A cool infographic tells a story visually — an engaging story built with your data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than just using pictures or colorful charts, infographics create the type of visual information that your audience will quickly grasp and remember. The emphasis is on building an engaging story from data rather than decorative visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure information into a simple 3-part story
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure information into a simple 3-part story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize content so it follows a clear, simple narrative (three parts) to make the message easy to follow and retain. This is presented as a core principle of what makes infographics work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify the design process and follow infographic design rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the design process and follow infographic design rules
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and follow a repeatable design process and the established rules of infographic design; the site/book explains fundamentals for both novices and experienced professionals to ensure effective results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend data visualizations with text, illustrations and images
rubrics_metrics.description: Blend data visualizations with text, illustrations and images to tell a complete story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine charts, explanatory text, illustrations, and images so the visualization and supporting elements work together to communicate the full message rather than relying on a single form of representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate visualization types and complex representations when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Use charts, illustrations, diagrams, maps, and complex representations of data as appropriate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select visualization types (charts, diagrams, maps, etc.) that suit the data and message; InfoNewt emphasizes innovative visualization techniques and complex representations where they aid communication. These designs can be adapted across multiple final formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose suitable final formats for distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Infographics and visual designs are used in a number of different final formats; infographics, presentations, posters, handouts, brochures, white papers, websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design with the intended final medium(s) in mind — online, print, presentations, collateral, or web content — since format affects layout, resolution, interactivity, and how the story is consumed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement a complete infographic release strategy to maximize SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a complete infographic release strategy to maximize SEO results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan distribution and promotional steps (release strategy) to increase visibility and search engine impact; consider SEO best practices alongside design to ensure the infographic reaches and is discoverable by the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design personal infographic resumes for self-marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Design a personal infographic resume to market yourself
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply infographic design principles to create a resume that visually markets skills and experience — useful as a personal branding and marketing tool.
